text: Does LDN lose it's effectiveness over the long term? LDN is one of the treatments that I started on pretty quickly after being diagnosed with CFS.  When I first titrated up to the 4.5mg dose I felt absolutely amazing.  My sleep was incredibly refreshing, my brain fog was gone, I was very energetic and motivated, and at work I was really engaged and practically dancing while working at the computer. Have you seen this thread:
Vitamin D may be vital for the efficacy of low-dose naltrexone (LDN)
That is a somewhat speculative thread, but conceivably if your vitamin D status changes, you might lose LDN efficacy. Note that it takes several weeks of vitamin D supplementation to get blood levels up.
